newsitem.title: USA: Canadian spot natgas drifts lower ahead of weekend.
newsitem.headline: Canadian spot natgas drifts lower ahead of weekend.

text.p: Canadian spot natural gas prices drifted lower again Friday due to mild temperatures and an expected drop in demand over the long holiday weekend, sources said.

At AECO storage hub, prices fell another 18 cents to the C$1.40-1.45 per gigajoule (GJ) range, as forecasters called for a high of nine degrees Celsius in Calgary on Saturday. Mild weather is expected to continue through early next week.
March AECO continued to falter, slipping by about six cents to the C$1.53-1.55 per GJ area. April/October AECO was talked around C$1.39.
At Sumas, Wash., prices plummeted into the $1.45-1.50 per million British thermal units (mmBtu) range, down about 20 cents from Thursday.
Sources attributed the softness to mild weather in the West, significantly weaker California prices and an abundant supply of hydroelectric power in the Northwest.
At Niagara, prices fell by about 10 cents to about $2.40 per mmBtu, ladened by milder weather and ample storage supplies.
Canadian Gas Association said Friday that gas stocks in the East as of Feb 7 were at 72.91 bcf, or 31.35 percent of capacity. These data compare with year-ago levels at 19.8 percent full.
